name: subprocess-output-tail-copy
reason: H5, MEASURED 2026-09-27 by tests/aukora-subprocess-output-retention.test.mjs: OutputCollector.push trims its head chunk with `head.subarray(excess)`, and Buffer.subarray returns a VIEW sharing the parent's backing store. A retained window of 1024 B therefore PINS A 1048576 B ALLOCATION (x1024 amplification) while the collector's own byte counter reports 1024 B — which is why the leak is invisible in its own accounting. In the alpha-17 snapshot pair this was the ONLY one of the reviewed roots that grew: across 120 driven turns Session (H1) and projection (H2) were unchanged, `chunks` grew, and Buffer 12.66 MB / ArrayBuffer 12.30 MB were the largest retained structures in a 50 MB heap. The fix copies the trimmed tail so it stops pinning the whole parent allocation; MEASURED on a copy of the module, the same window then pins a pooled 8192 B slab — x128 less.
